verses.text: Then Job answered:
"Listen closely to what I say. If you want to comfort me, start by listening.
Give me a chance to speak. After I've finished, you can go back to mocking me.
Is my complaint against a human being? Why shouldn't I be impatient?
Look at me and be appalled. Put your hand over your mouth.
When I think about it, I'm shaken, and my whole body trembles with horror.
Why do wicked people live on, grow old, and gain power?
They see their children firmly established around them, their descendants right in front of them.
Their homes are safe from fear, and God's rod never strikes them.
Their bulls breed without fail. Their cows give birth without miscarrying.
They send their little ones out like a flock, and their children dance.
They sing to the tambourine and harp and celebrate to the sound of the flute.
They live out their days in prosperity and go down to Sheol in an instant.
Yet they tell God, 'Leave us alone. We don't want to know your ways.
Who is the Almighty that we should serve him? What would we gain by praying to him?'
Their prosperity is beyond their own control. I want nothing to do with the plans of the wicked.
How often does the lamp of the wicked actually go out? How often does disaster overtake them, or God deal out suffering in his anger?
How often are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away in a storm?
You say, 'God saves up the punishment for their children.' Let him repay the wrongdoer directly so they know what they've done.
Let their own eyes see their destruction. Let them drink the anger of the Almighty.
What do they care what happens to their household after them, once their allotted months are cut short?
Can anyone teach God anything, when he judges even those in the highest places?
One person dies in full strength, completely comfortable and at peace.
Their pails are full of milk, and the marrow in their bones is moist.
Another dies bitter at heart, having never tasted anything good.
They lie down side by side in the dust, and worms cover them both.
I know what you're thinking and what you're plotting to do to me.
You ask, 'Where is the ruler's house now? Where is the tent where the wicked lived?'
Haven't you asked people who travel the roads? Don't you know what they've seen,
that an evil person is kept for the day of disaster and led away on the day of wrath?
Who confronts them about their conduct? Who repays them for what they've done?
Even so, they're carried to the grave, and people keep watch over their tomb.
The soil of the valley lies sweet upon them. A crowd follows after them, just as countless people went before them.
How can you comfort me with nonsense when all that's left of your answers is falsehood?"
